name: Cefuroxime
executiveSummary: 2nd-generation cephalosporin. Adult IV **750 mg–1.5 g every 8 h**. Pediatrics **75–150 mg/kg/day every 8 h** (meningitis up to **240 mg/kg/day**). Neonates: **50–100 mg/kg/day** divided every 8–12 h by GA/weight.
indications:
## Indications

- Respiratory, ENT, urinary, skin/soft-tissue, bone infections by susceptible organisms (incl. *H. influenzae*, E. coli, Klebsiella).
- Selected surgical prophylaxis.

## Precautions

- Beta-lactam allergy. Adjust in CKD.
- Not first choice for *H. influenzae* meningitis (prefer 3rd gen).

> IV or PO per presentation.

adulto.presentation: Vial 750 mg, 1.5 g IV; tablets 250–500 mg PO.
adulto.dose: IV: 750 mg–1.5 g every 8 h. PO: 250–500 mg every 12 h.

pediatrico.dose: Ages 3–12 years: 75–150 mg/kg/day every 8 h, max dose: 6 g/day; meningitis: 240 mg/kg/day, max dose: 9 g/day; ≥13 years and adults: 750–1500 mg/dose every 8 h, max dose: 6 g/day. Adult preoperative dose: 1.5 g.
pediatrico.notes: Not advised in meningitis due to Haemophilus influenzae. Adjust dose in renal impairment.

neonatal.dose: **50–100 mg/kg/day IV** divided every **8–12 h** by gestational age and weight (non-meningeal infections). Meningitis: prefer other cephalosporins — if used, high regimens infectious diseases/NICU only.

stability:
## Stability

- Diluted IV: 24 h refrigerated.

## Pediatric guide

- 24 h at room temperature and 48 h refrigerated between 4 °C and 8 °C.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Neutropenia, hemolytic anemia, headache, C. difficile colitis, injection-site phlebitis, rash, anal pruritus.
